label: l / r / 3 input mid-way through the original phase, boosted by earlier u/v/w/o
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at steps 2-8 (mostly t=3-5); never at t=0-1, the delimiter, or the copy phase. Driven by the input token: l (13x lift, ~49% of mass), r (8x, ~26%), 3 (5x, ~14%), with weaker 2 and s. The token alone gives poor precision (only ~13% of l inputs fire). Firing is much more likely, and the largest activations occur, when u, v, w or o appeared earlier in the prefix (top examples look like u v w l, a w w o l). Mostly first occurrences of the token. The predicate (l/r/3 at t=2-6 with an earlier u/v/w/o) gets dev F1 about 0.50 and mass recall about 0.69. The remaining context dependence looks graded rather than captured by a clean rule.
